title: Every harness schema that cites an incident id takes the incident record's own id pattern

looked_in: grep for 'INC-' in contracts/schemas/harness_*.schema.json at 1c27af54: the id pattern appears in three schemas, and HP-013 widened one
the expect-fail run at 1c27af54: check89_harness_incident_machine_word_not_its_seats fails check 1 three times beside its check 89 line
a probe bundle outside the tree: a retro naming INC-20261022-scope-01 is refused by harness_retro.schema.json

changes.change: answers[] and classification.members_found[] take the pattern ^INC-([0-9]{8}|undated)-([a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z][a-z0-9]*)*-)?[0-9]{2}$, the incident schema's own.

So the three cannot drift again: either one definition the other two reference, or a check 89 line that the three patterns are equal. Either is a reshape; the builder picks what check 1's schema loading supports.
It then fails check 89 alone; its three check 1 lines go. An accepted control beside it: a retro and a proposal naming a machine-word incident pass check 1.

fixtures.path: an accepted bundle: INC-20261022-scope-01 recorded by harness-scope-20261019-1 and named in retro/20261022-scope.json's new_incidents and in a proposal's answers

reach.how_they_learn: Until HP-014 lands, both seats keep the old id form and the interim number split (office 01-49, scope 50-99); a retro file may already carry the machine word. This seat says so to the scope seat through the intake seats of both computers.
reach.use_site: check 1, at the commit of a retro or proposal that cites a machine-word id

notes: Completes HP-013: no rule changes, only the same key shape in the two schemas that cite the key. What this seat watched failing before is the probe bundle at 1c27af54, outside the tree; the builder watches its own committed fixture.
